title: Fine motor skills in patients with haemophilia: A case-control study including psychometric evaluation
summary:
Haemophilia is a condition in which the blood does not clot properly. This can lead to bleeding in the muscles and joints – even with good medical treatment. The elbow joints are particularly often affected.
So far, many studies have mainly focused on how haemophilia affects the legs. However, much less is known about how the arms and hands are impacted, especially when it comes to fine motor skills like writing or gripping – particularly in adults.
One study with children showed that nearly three-quarters of them had difficulty writing, compared to only about 10–30% of healthy children.
This study aims to find out:
How well people with haemophilia can perform fine motor tasks – compared to healthy individuals.
How these abilities are related to hand grip strength, tissue flexibility in the forearm, and joint health.
Whether a specific test – the Moberg Pick-Up Test – is reliable for detecting such limitations in people with haemophilia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with haemophilia
Inclusion criteria:
- 18 years of age or older
- suffering from moderate or severe hemophilia A or B
- submitted written informed consent

Healthy controls
Inclusion criteria:
- men 18 years of age or older
- submitted written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with haemophilia
Exclusion criteria:
- other bleeding disorders
- surgeries of the elbows up to six month before assessment
- suffering from different rheumatologic diseases like M. Bechterev, Psorioasis or other local or generalized joint infections (borreliosis, septic arthritis), (diabetic) neuropathy, other neurological disorders
- recent bleedings of the upper extremities within 10 days before assessment

Healthy controls
Exclusion criteria:
- surgeries of the elbows up to six month before assessment
- suffering from different rheumatologic diseases like M. Bechterev, Psorioasis or other local or generalized joint infections (borreliosis, septic arthritis), bleeding disorders, (diabetic) neuropathy, other neurological disorders, orthopedic impairments in joints of the upper extremities
